body.translated_text: <s>Sabhikasaugataśāsanapravrajyāvratacaraṇaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on Going Forth, Vows, and Practice in the Buddhist Teaching with a Debate)

children.translated_text: (SAM 4Ob4: additional verses)
Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, wishing to hear more excellent words,

children.text: upaguptaṃ yatiṃ natvā sāñjalir evam abravīt // Svp_*1* //
children.translated_text: bowing to the ascetic <s>Upagupta</s>, spoke thus with joined palms: (*1*)

children.text: bhadanta śrotum icchāmi punas tasya jagadguroḥ /
children.translated_text: "Venerable sir, I wish to hear again of that teacher of the world,
the power of the chief of sages—please instruct me about that." (*2*)

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ rājñā śrutvā so 'rhan yatiḥ sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this request made by the king, that worthy ascetic, the wise one,

children.text: taṃ narendraṃ samāmantrya saṃpaśyann evam ādiśat // Svp_*3* //
children.translated_text: addressing that lord of men, gazing upon him, instructed thus: (*3*)
(SAM 40b6; BKA C 99b4; BKA T 71b8)

children.text: atha śṛṇu samādhāya yathā me guruṇoditaṃ /
children.translated_text: "Now listen with concentration; as it was told by my teacher,
so I shall relate it, for the increase of your merit. (1)
In the great city of <s>Mathurā</s> there was a great man,
a merchant named <s>Sādhubhoga</s>, endowed with abundance of all goods. (2)
His wife was beautiful-limbed, lovely, resembling <s>Rati</s> (goddess of love),
virtuous, of appearance like <s>Śrī</s> (goddess of fortune), the excellent one named <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>. (3)
To her was born a girl called <s>Triyantrikā</s>, afflicted with bodily deformity,

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dārikāṃ mātā babhūva vyāhatāśayā || 4 ||
children.translated_text: and seeing that girl, the mother became distressed in mind. (4)
The father too, upon seeing that girl <s>Triyantrikā</s>,
stood with his heart torn by shame, absorbed in sighing. (5)

children.text: tataḥ sa janakaḥ śreṣṭhī nimittajñān vicakṣaṇān /
children.translated_text: Then that father, the merchant, hastily summoned
skilled soothsayers and <s>tīrthikas</s> (sectarian teachers) and showed them the girl. (6)

children.text: triyantritāṃ śiśuṃ dṛṣṭvā nimittajñaḥ sa tīrthikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the child with three bends, the soothsayer, that <s>tīrthika</s>,
announced before the merchant: 'This girl is inauspicious.' (7)
Hearing that, the father, the merchant, his mind agitated by grief and apprehension,
his soul scorched by the fire of affection and sorrow, stood with senses bewildered. (8)

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sā satī bhāryā śrutvā tat tīrthikoditaṃ /
children.translated_text: Seeing her and hearing the words spoken by the <s>tīrthika</s>,
his virtuous wife too, scorched by the fire of affection and sorrow, became distressed in mind. (9)
At that moment, a <s>parivrājikā</s> (wandering nun) of highly meritorious soul, skilled in all branches of learning,
came to the merchant's house and attended upon them. (10)

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā samupāyātāṃ śreṣṭhī sa sahasotthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing her arrived, the merchant quickly rose,
respectfully greeted her and seated her on a clean seat. (11)

children.text: sādhubhogas tataḥ śreṣṭhī tāṃ parivrājikāṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: Then the merchant <s>Sādhubhoga</s>, with joy, having honored
that <s>parivrājikā</s> (wandering nun) and fed her, and having pleased her, spoke thus: (12)
'Good lady, a girl has been born to me, my own daughter, with three bends;

children.text: imāṃ te dātum icchāmi samanvāhartum arhasi || 13 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to give her to you—please accept her.' (13)

children.text: iti nivedya sa śreṣṭhī samādāya nijāṃ sutāṃ /
children.translated_text: Having announced this, the merchant took his own daughter

children.text: tāṃ tasyāḥ purataḥ sthāpya bahu dravyaṃ ca prabravīt || 14 ||
children.translated_text: and placed her before the nun, along with much wealth, and said: (14)

children.text: iyaṃ me dārikā bhadre bhavatyai saṃkalpitā mayā /
children.translated_text: 'This is my girl, good lady; she has been dedicated to you by me;

children.text: tad bhavatyā samādāya saṃpālyā svātmajā yathā || 15 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, having taken her, please raise her as your own daughter. (15)
You are without sons or daughters, without a husband, free from entanglements;

children.text: tasmāt tvayā pālanīyā svātmajeva śiśur iyaṃ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: therefore this child should be cared for by you as your very own daughter. (16)'

children.text: iti nivedya sa śreṣṭhī sadhātrīṃ tāṃ sutāṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: Having announced this, the merchant joyfully gave his daughter along with a nurse
and accompanied by much wealth to her, and spoke again thus: (17)

children.text: yadeyaṃ saṃpravṛddhā syāt tadā te dāsikā bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'When she has grown up, she shall be your servant;

children.text: tasmād yāvad iyaṃ bālā tāvat pālyā tvayā sadā || 18 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, as long as she is a child, she must always be cared for by you. (18)

children.text: tataḥ pravrājya sve dharme saṃcārayasva sanmate /
children.translated_text: Then, having given her the going-forth, train her in your own <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: adhyāpaya ca sarvāṇi śāstrāṇy api yathākramaṃ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: and teach her all the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures) in due order. (19)'

children.text: ity uktvā sa pitā putrīṃ vastrālaṃkāramaṇḍitām /
children.translated_text: Having said this, the father adorned his daughter with garments and ornaments

children.text: tāṃ tasyai brahmacāriṇyai saṃkalpya pradadau muda || 20 ||
children.translated_text: and joyfully dedicated and gave her to that <s>brahmacāriṇī</s> (celibate woman). (20)
Having taken the one thus given, along with the nurse and attendants,

children.text: datvā bhadrāśiṣaṃ tasmai śirī nāmā tato 'carat* || 21 ||
children.translated_text: and having given her auspicious blessings to him, the one named <s>Śirī</s> then departed. (21)

children.text: tatra sā svāśrame gatvā sadhātrīṃ tāṃ pramoditā /
children.translated_text: Going to her own hermitage, she was delighted, and with the nurse
she quickly nurtured her, caring for her as her own daughter. (22)
Thus being cared for, she grew day by day,
her faculties fully nourished—she became lovely, captivating all minds. (23)
Then, under the instruction of that [nun], she was given the going-forth according to the proper rite,
and having adopted the ascetic's restraint, she went about wearing the saffron robe. (24)

children.text: tataḥ sā sumatī kanyā sarvā lipīr aśikṣata /
children.translated_text: Then that intelligent girl <s>Sumatī</s> learned all scripts,
and then gradually she studied all the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures). (25)
Having thus studied, that wise one, who had reached the far shore of all knowledge,
came to be named '<s>Mahādhī</s>' (Great Intelligence) on account of her great wisdom—she who was <s>Triyantrikā</s>. (26)
Gradually, she of crooked limbs became as tall as a <s>śāla</s> tree, being wise,
for through the power of her own <s>dharma</s>, her former sins had been exhausted. (27)
Having mastered the sixty-four arts, skilled in the study of the <s>Vedas</s>,
she shone forth, striking terror into the minds of all debaters. (28)

children.text: sarve 'pi vādino vijñās tāṃ jetuṃ naiva śekire /
children.translated_text: All the skilled debaters were unable to defeat her;
she herself, having vanquished all disputants, reigned supreme. (29)
The fragrance of her fame spread in all directions;
hearing of that <s>Sumatī</s>, everyone was filled with great wonder. (30)
Then there arrived a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who had mastered all the <s>Vedānta</s>,
a proud one named <s>Vidyākara</s>, coming from the south. (31)
He wrapped his side with a copper plate and, with his mind exalted,

children.text: ulkām ujvālitāṃ dhṛtvā pure tatra mudāviśat || 32 ||
children.translated_text: holding a burning torch, entered that city with delight. (32)

children.text: yo mayā saha saṃvādaṃ kartum atra samicchati /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever wishes to engage in a debate with me here,
I shall approach him'—so the proud one went about proclaiming. (33)
Seeing him arrive, the great people of <s>Mathurā</s>

children.text: taṃ dvijaṃ samupāmantrya sarve py evaṃ babhāṣire || 34 ||
children.translated_text: greeted that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and all spoke thus: (34)

children.text: sādho mātra samāgaccha dhṛtvolkāṃ jvalitām imāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Good sir, do not approach [others] carrying this burning torch;

children.text: yā parivrājikā sādhvī sā prājñā vidyate satī || 35 ||
children.translated_text: there is here a <s>parivrājikā</s> (wandering nun), a virtuous and wise one indeed.' (35)
Hearing those words, <s>Vidyākara</s>, exceedingly proud,
approached the people of <s>Mathurā</s> and spoke arrogantly: (36)
'Who is this wise <s>parivrājikā</s>? Where is she to be found?

children.text: tām ahaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi tad darśayitum arhathaḥ || 37 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to see her—please show her to me.' (37)

children.text: iti taduktam ākarṇya sarve 'pi te mahājanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing those words spoken by him, all those great people,

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ samālokya saṃpraṣṭum evam abravīt || 38 ||
children.translated_text: looking at that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, spoke thus to question him: (38)

children.text: sādho yadi tayā sārdhaṃ saṃvādaṃ kartum icchasi /
children.translated_text: 'Good sir, if you wish to engage in a debate with her,

children.text: tāṃ kāntāṃ sumatiṃ vijñāṃ darśayiṣyāmahe vayaṃ || 39 ||
children.translated_text: we will show you that lovely, wise <s>Sumatī</s>.' (39)

children.text: iti sarvair api proktaṃ śrutvā sa brāhmaṇo mudā /
children.translated_text: Hearing what was said by all of them, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> joyfully,

children.text: saṃpaśyans tān janān sarvān puraḥ sthitvaivam abravīt || 40 ||
children.translated_text: gazing at all those people, stood before them and spoke thus: (40)

children.text: bho bhavantas tayā sārdhaṃ saṃvādaṃ kartum utsahe /
children.translated_text: 'Sirs! I am eager to engage in a debate with her;

children.text: tad enāṃ samupānīya darśayantu puro mama || 41 ||
children.translated_text: therefore bring her and show her before me.' (41)

children.text: iti tena samākhyātaṃ śrutvā tatheti te janāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing what was said by him, those people [said] 'So be it!' and

children.text: sahasā tatrāśrame gatvā tasyā yater upāśrayan || 42 ||
children.translated_text: quickly went to her hermitage and approached that ascetic woman. (42)

children.text: tān vīkṣya samupāsīnān sā parivrājikā mudā /
children.translated_text: Seeing them seated nearby, that <s>parivrājikā</s> (wandering nun) joyfully
asked: 'For what purpose have you come?' (43)

children.text: tac chrutvā te janāḥ sarve natvā sāṃjalayo mudā /
children.translated_text: Hearing that, all those people, bowing with joined palms, joyfully,

children.text: tāṃ mahādhiyam āpaśyan māthurā evam abruvan || 44 ||
children.translated_text: gazing upon that <s>Mahādhī</s> (Great Intelligence), the people of <s>Mathurā</s> spoke thus: (44)
'A learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is here, skilled in all <s>śāstras</s>,
one who has mastered the <s>Vedānta</s>, wise, having come from the south. (45)

children.text: tat tena saha saṃvādaṃ kartuṃ yadi tvam icchasi /
children.translated_text: If you wish to engage in a debate with him,
display your qualities in the midst of the assembly of all people. (46)

children.text: śaknosi yadi vijñena saṃvādaṃ kuru mānini /
children.translated_text: If you are able, O proud one, engage in debate with that wise one;

children.text: parājitā cet tena tvaṃ vayam apy upahāsyatāṃ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: but if you are defeated by him, we too shall be objects of ridicule.' (47)

children.text: iti tair uktam ākarṇya sā parivrājikā sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing those words spoken by them, that wise <s>parivrājikā</s> [said:]

children.text: vāḍham icchāmi saṃvādaṃ kartuṃ tena dvijena hi || 48 ||
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, I wish to engage in debate with that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! (48)
In the midst of the assembly of all people I shall display my qualities.'

children.text: iti tayā samuditaṃ śrutvā sarve savismayāḥ || 49 ||
children.translated_text: Hearing her declaration, all were filled with amazement. (49)

children.text: sarveme tat pravṛttāntaṃ rājñaḥ puro nyavedayan /
children.translated_text: They all reported this matter before the king;

children.text: tat samākarṇya rājā sa yathāmūbhyāṃ prabhāṣitaṃ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: hearing what had been spoken by those two, that king [said:] (50)

children.text: kārayata tathā yūyam iti tān avadaj janān /
children.translated_text: 'Let it be done as you arrange'—thus he addressed those people.

children.text: tadanujñāṃ samāsādya sarve te muditā janāḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained his permission, all those people were delighted, (51)

children.text: āmantrya tajjanān etad vṛttaṃ proktvaivam ūcire /
children.translated_text: and having invited those people and reported this event, they announced thus:
'With this most learned <s>parivrājikā</s>, (52)

children.text: amuko brāhmaṇo vidvān saṃvādaṃ kartum icchati /
children.translated_text: a certain learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> wishes to engage in debate;

children.text: tac chrotuṃ ye 'bhivāñcchanti jñātuṃ caitad viśeṣatāṃ || 53 ||
children.translated_text: those who wish to hear this and to learn of this distinction, (53)

children.text: sarve tatra samāyāntu pure 'taḥ saptame dine /
children.translated_text: let them all assemble here in the city on the seventh day hence.'
Thus commanded by the king, [the heralds] proclaimed on all sides: (Svp 54)
"Having sounded the bell, urge the good people forward!"

children.text: iti tatkathitaṃ śrutvā sarve 'pi sajjanā mudā || 55 ||
children.translated_text: Having heard what was thus spoken, all the good people with joy (Svp 55)

children.text: tatra te muditāḥ sarve yathādiṣṭaṃ mahībhṛtā /
children.translated_text: were all delighted there, as instructed by the king.

children.text: tathā ghaṇṭāṃ samunnādya sarvāṃl lokān vyanodayan // Svp_*55* //
children.translated_text: Thus, having sounded the bell loudly, they urged all the people [to gather]. (Svp *55*)
Having pledged "so be it," they caused the bell to be sounded.
Having heard that, all the good people dwelling in <s>Mathurā</s> (Svp 56)
proceeded forth, desiring to hear and see that debate.
Then <s>Vidyākara</s>, the proud [scholar], thought thus in his mind: (Svp 57)
"What sort of expert in learning is that wise female wanderer (<s>parivrājikā</s>)?"

children.text: iti vicintya satrasthas tāṃ parivrājikāṃ satīṃ || 58 ||
children.translated_text: Having thought thus, anxious [to know], [he went] to [see] that virtuous female wanderer — (Svp 58)

children.text: draṣṭuṃ tatrāśrame gatvā lokān evam apṛcchata /
children.translated_text: going to the hermitage there to see [her], he asked the people thus:

children.text: yā parivrājikā prājñā sā kā kuhasamāśritā || 59 ||
children.translated_text: "The wise female wanderer — who is she, and in what dwelling does she reside? (Svp 59)

children.text: tāṃ bhavantaḥ samāmantrya saṃdarśayantu me drutaṃ /
children.translated_text: You good people, having called upon her, show her to me quickly."
Having heard what was thus spoken, those dwelling nearby (Svp 60)
called upon that virtuous female wanderer and spoke thus:

children.text: bho bhadre brāhmaṇo vidvān bhavatīṃ draṣṭum icchati || 61 ||
children.translated_text: "O good lady, a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> wishes to see you. (Svp 61)

children.text: tad bhavatī tam āmantrya saṃdarśayatu sādaraṃ /
children.translated_text: Please call upon him and show yourself to him respectfully."

children.text: iti taduktam ākarṇya sā parivrājikā mudā || 62 ||
children.translated_text: Having heard what was thus spoken, that female wanderer with delight (Svp 62)
called upon that learned man and seated herself before him.
Seeing that female wanderer — beautiful, charming, exceedingly lovely — (Svp 63)
he stood [gazing] for a long time, his heart ablaze with the fire of passion.

children.text: sā parivrājikā cāpi dṛṣṭvā taṃ sundaraṃ dvijaṃ || 64 ||
children.translated_text: And that female wanderer too, seeing that handsome twice-born (<s>dvija</s>), (Svp 64)
with her heart agitated by passion, sat down even as she gazed [at him].
Between those two, by the working of fate, the fire of passion arose, (Svp 65)
and their hearts being consumed by it, they became attached through affection.

children.text: tataḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ kānto yuvā rāgākulendriyaḥ || 66 ||
children.translated_text: Then that handsome young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, his senses agitated by passion, (Svp 66)

children.text: tāṃ kāntāṃ yauvanīṃ rāmāṃ saṃpaśyan raha abravīt /
children.translated_text: gazing at that beautiful youthful woman, spoke privately:

children.text: ayi bhadre subhadrāṃgi tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā mama mānasaṃ || 67 ||
children.translated_text: "O fair one, of lovely limbs! Seeing you, in my mind (Svp 67)

children.text: rāgāgnir dīpyate dagdhuṃ tac chamīkartum arhati /
children.translated_text: the fire of passion blazes to consume [me] — you should quench it.

children.text: yadi te 'sti dayā bhadre brāhmaṇe 'smin vicakṣaṇe || 68 ||
children.translated_text: If you have compassion, O fair one, for this discerning <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, (Svp 68)
then look upon me with a kind gaze, comfort me and make me happy."

children.text: iti taduktam ākarṇya sā parivrājikā api || 69 ||
children.translated_text: Having heard what was thus spoken, that female wanderer too, (Svp 69)
her heart muddied by desire and passion, stood as if bewildered.

children.text: evaṃ saṃmohitasvāntāṃ tāṃ vīkṣya brāhmaṇo 'pi saḥ || 70 ||
children.translated_text: Seeing her thus with a bewildered heart, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too (Svp 70)
embraced [her], looked at her with beautiful eyes, and comforting [her], spoke thus:

children.text: ayi bhadre yadi te 'sti snehamaitramano mayi || 71 ||
children.translated_text: "O fair one, if you have affection and friendly feeling toward me, (Svp 71)
having heard my spoken words, let your heart rejoice.

children.text: sumate yan mayā sārdhaṃ vivādaṃ kartum icchasi || 72 ||
children.translated_text: O wise one, [I know] you desire to hold a debate with me — (Svp 72)

children.text: aham api tvayā sārdhaṃ vivādaṃ kartum utsahe /
children.translated_text: I too am eager to hold a debate with you.

children.text: tad yadi te mayi snehas tan me hitaṃ vacaḥ śṛṇu || 73 ||
children.translated_text: So if you have affection for me, hear my beneficial words: (Svp 73)
having set [them] in your mind, you should act accordingly."
Having heard what was thus spoken, the exceedingly wise one, afflicted by desire, (Svp 74)
looking at <s>Vidyākara</s>, spoke thus with a smile:

children.text: bho dvijendra mahāprājña samādiṣṭaṃ tvayā yathā || 75 ||
children.translated_text: "O best of twice-born, O greatly wise one, as commanded by you, (Svp 75)

children.text: tathāhaṃ kartum icchāmi satyam iti pravakṣyatāṃ /
children.translated_text: so I wish to do — let it be spoken as truth."

children.text: iti tayā samākhyātaṃ śrutvāsau cāturo mudā || 76 ||
children.translated_text: Having heard what was thus declared by her, that clever one joyfully (Svp 76)
spoke to her with a smiling face, trembling with the passion of love:

children.text: yady evaṃ kriyate rāme tathāvayoḥ samāgamaṃ || 77 ||
children.translated_text: "If this be done, O lovely one, then our union — (Svp 77)

children.text: yāvaj jīvaṃ sukhaṃ bhuktvā ramamāṇau caremahi /
children.translated_text: enjoying happiness as long as we live, let us go about in delight.

children.text: tad abhisamayaṃ kṛtvā guptam āvāṃ vidhāya tat || 78 ||
children.translated_text: Having made a compact and having arranged [it] secretly between us, (Svp 78)
we shall discourse thus in the midst of the assembly:

children.text: yo 'tra vivādite jetā tasya sa hatamānikaḥ || 79 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whoever is the winner in this debate — the loser, with pride defeated, (Svp 79)
having taken refuge and discipleship, shall always be the other's follower.'
Having made this compact and having made the great assembly witnesses, (Svp 80)
we shall debate with each other there in the midst of the entire assembly.

children.text: mayā cen nirjitā tvaṃ strī tadā loke na ninditā || 81 ||
children.translated_text: If I defeat you, a woman — then in the world you shall not be criticized: (Svp 81)

children.text: kim āścaryaṃ jitā bālā puṃsā sateti vakṣyate /
children.translated_text: 'What wonder? A young woman was defeated by a man' — so they will say.

children.text: yadi tatra sabhāmadhye nirjito 'haṃ tvayā striyā || 82 ||
children.translated_text: But if there in the midst of the assembly I am defeated by you, a woman, (Svp 82)
then I shall become one condemned by all in the world, everywhere.

children.text: pumān api dvijaḥ prājño bālayāpi striyā jitaḥ || 83 ||
children.translated_text: 'A man, a twice-born, wise — yet defeated even by a young woman!' — (Svp 83)
Thus I, <s>Vidyākara</s>, of great renown, would become an object of ridicule.

children.text: iti tvayā tadā tatra saṃvāde nau pravartite || 84 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the debate between us is conducted there by you, (Svp 84)

children.text: ante pratyuttaraṃ naiva dātavyam api kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: at the end, you should not give any further reply at all.

children.text: tathā jitvā mayā tvaṃ strī śiṣyāpi me bhaves tadā || 85 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having won, [when] I [have defeated] you, a woman — you would also be my disciple. (Svp 85)

children.text: evaṃ samāgamaṃ nau syād vāvaj jīvaṃ sukhaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: In this way our union would be [established], and great happiness as long as we live."
Having heard what was thus spoken, she, burning with desire and passion, (Svp 86)
having agreed saying "so be it," dismissed that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sa brāhmaṇas tatra kṛtvābhisamayaṃ tayā /
children.translated_text: Thus that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> there, having made the compact with her,
unobserved by the people, went to his own dwelling with delight. (Svp 87)
Then on another day, in the morning, the learned one, eager with desire,
going to the midst of the great public assembly, called [them] and spoke thus: (Svp 88)
"Good people, today with that female wanderer

children.text: saṃvādaṃ kartum icchāmi tad ānayantu tāṃ drutaṃ || 89 ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hold a debate — bring her here quickly!" (Svp 89)

children.text: iti tenoditaṃ śrutvā sarve 'pi te mahājanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard what he thus said, all those great people

children.text: tatheti samupāmantrya tāṃ yatim evam abruvan || 90 ||
children.translated_text: having agreed saying "so be it," addressed that female ascetic (<s>yati</s>) thus: (Svp 90)
"Lady, this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, expert in all <s>śāstras</s>,

children.text: bhavatyā saha saṃvādaṃ kartum adya samicchati || 91 ||
children.translated_text: today wishes to hold a debate with you. (Svp 91)
If you wish to debate with him,
come to that arena, in the midst of the assembly, and take your stand." (Svp 92)

children.text: iti taduktam ākarṇya sā parivrājikā mudā /
children.translated_text: Having heard what was thus spoken, that female wanderer with joy,
desiring that [man as her] husband, took her seat in the arena. (Svp 93)
And <s>Vidyākara</s> too, having come there to the arena, the seat of the assembly,
looking at [her] with a greatly wise face, joyfully took his seat. (Svp 94)

children.text: tatra raṃge sabhāmadhye tāv ubhau samupāśritau /
children.translated_text: When those two were seated there in the arena, in the midst of the assembly,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā śrutvāpi te sarve mahājanā upāśrayan || 95 ||
children.translated_text: all the great people, having seen and heard, [also] took their seats. (Svp 95)

children.text: tad draṣṭuṃ kautukākrāntaṃ viprāś ca brahmacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: To see that [debate], seized with curiosity — <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and celibate students,
people led by the king — all assembled there. (Svp 96)
And likewise other good people — artisans, merchants, common folk, and others —

children.text: sarve 'tra samupāyātās tad draṣṭuṃ samupāśrayan // Svp_*96* //
children.translated_text: all came there and took their seats to watch. (Svp *96*)

children.text: tān draṣṭuṃ samupāsīnān sarvāṃl lokān samīkṣya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing all those people seated to watch, that

children.text: brāhmaṇa utthitaḥ paśyan sāñjalir evam abravīt || 97 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> rose, and gazing [at them], spoke thus with joined palms: (Svp 97)
"Good people, the childish arrogance born of excessive pride

children.text: kṛtaṃ vaṭukacāpalyaṃ kartum arhantu tat kṣamāṃ || 98 ||
children.translated_text: that has been committed by us — please forgive that. (Svp 98)

children.text: yadi mayā vivāde 'tra nārīyaṃ nirjitā tadā /
children.translated_text: If in this debate I defeat this woman, then

children.text: kim āścaryaṃ vadel lokaḥ puṃsā nārī jiteti ca || 99 ||
children.translated_text: the world would say: 'What wonder? A woman was defeated by a man!' (Svp 99)

children.text: yady etayā striyāpy atra vivāde 'haṃ vinirjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: If by this woman, even here in the debate, I am defeated —

children.text: pumān api jito nāryā hīti syāṃ sarvaninditaḥ || 100 ||
children.translated_text: 'A man defeated by a woman, alas!' — I would be condemned by all. (Svp 100)

children.text: tad atra samayaṃ kṛtvā vivādaṃ kartum utsahe /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, having made a compact, I am eager to hold the debate.

children.text: tad bhavanto 'pi madhyasthā draṣṭum arhantu sādhavaḥ || 101 ||
children.translated_text: You good people too, being impartial, please watch as arbiters. (Svp 101)

children.text: yady eṣātra vivāde māṃ parājetuṃ hi śaknuyāt /
children.translated_text: If she here in the debate is able to defeat me,
I shall attain discipleship under her and be her constant follower. (Svp 102)

children.text: yady atrāham imāṃ jitvā jayaśriyaṃ samāpnuyāṃ /
children.translated_text: If here I, having defeated her, should attain the glory of victory,

children.text: mama śiṣyatvam āsādya bhaved eṣā sadānugā || 103 ||
children.translated_text: she shall attain discipleship under me and be my constant follower." (Svp 103)

children.text: iti saṃprārthya vipro 'sau tāṃ parivrājikāṃ satīṃ /
children.translated_text: Having thus proposed, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, to the virtuous female wanderer,
looking [at her], asked a question of grammar and challenged her. (Svp 104)
In response to that, that wise female wanderer
having defeated that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, astonished the assembly. (Svp 105)

children.text: tac chrutvā te janāḥ sarve vismayāpannamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard that, all those people, their minds struck with wonder,

children.text: prājñeyaṃ yatir ity uktvā svasvālayam upācaram || 106 ||
children.translated_text: saying 'This female ascetic is wise indeed!' — departed to their own dwellings. (Svp 106)

children.text: tat paredyus tathā tatra sā parivrājikāgatā /
children.translated_text: Then, on the next day, there again that female wanderer came,

children.text: te 'pi santo janāḥ sarve samāgatya samāśrayan || 107 ||
children.translated_text: and all those good people too, having assembled, took their seats. (Svp 107)

children.text: tataḥ sa brāhmaṇas tatra sabhāmadhye samāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having taken his seat there in the midst of the assembly,
looking at that female wanderer, questioned her on the meaning of the <s>śāstras</s>. (Svp 108)

children.text: tac chāstrārthaṃ samākhyāya yuvatir api sā sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Having explained that meaning of the scripture, she, the young woman, was also wise.

children.text: vidvāṃsam api taṃ jitvā sarvān sato 'nvamodayat || 109 ||
children.translated_text: Having defeated even that learned one, she delighted all the people present. || <s>Svp</s>_109 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca tṛtīye 'py ahni sā yoṣid api sanmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus on the third day also, that woman of good judgment
clearly expounded in the debate on all arts. || <s>Svp</s>_110 ||

children.text: evaṃ turyadine cāpi pañcame divase tathā /
children.translated_text: Thus on the fourth day too, and likewise on the fifth day,
on the sixth day as well, she thus taught the true meaning. || <s>Svp</s>_111 ||

children.text: evaṃ sa brāhmaṇas tatra saptame 'hni samāśrite /
children.translated_text: Thus that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having taken shelter there on the seventh day,
having made a binding agreement of action with her, approached the arena. || <s>Svp</s>_112 ||
As if with a mind overcome by shame, he spoke to the people in great distress:

children.text: adyāpy ahaṃ yadi jitas tasyāḥ syām anugo nanu || 113 ||
children.translated_text: "Even today, if I am defeated, I would surely become her follower." || <s>Svp</s>_113 ||

children.text: jeṣyati pratyahaṃ saivam ekasminn apy ahaṃ kimu /
children.translated_text: "She will win every day in the same way — how could I [win] even on a single [day]?

children.text: vāṇīcchalāj jitā sā tu yato yoṣit sarasvatī || 114 ||
children.translated_text: But she was defeated by a trick of speech, since that woman is [truly] <s>Sarasvatī</s>." || <s>Svp</s>_114 ||

children.text: iti proktvā dvijaḥ kāmī kāmāturīṃ mahādhiyaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the amorous <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [addressing] the love-struck, greatly intelligent woman,
questioned the lady of bold speech concerning <s>Vedānta</s>. || <s>Svp</s>_115 ||

children.text: tatra vijñāpi sā sādhvī smṛtvābhisamayaṃ sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that virtuous and wise woman, remembering the agreement,

children.text: api pratyuttaraṃ kiñcid asamarthaiva no dadau || 116 ||
children.translated_text: did not give even a single reply, being unable [by the terms of the pact]. || <s>Svp</s>_116 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ paśyan mahājanān sabhāśritān /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, seeing the great assembly of people seated in the hall,
with a joyful, well-pleased face, with joined palms, spoke thus: || <s>Svp</s>_117 ||

children.text: bhavanto dṛśyatām atra labhate ko jayaśriyaṃ /
children.translated_text: "O sirs, let it be seen here — who obtains the glory of victory?

children.text: iti samīkṣya prākhyātum arhanti mānyathā khalu || 118 ||
children.translated_text: Having examined this, you should declare it, and not otherwise." || <s>Svp</s>_118 ||

children.text: iti tat prārthitaṃ śrutvā sarve 'pi te sabhājanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard that request, all those assembly-members
praising that treasure of learning, the greatly wise one, spoke thus: || <s>Svp</s>_119 ||

children.text: kovidātra bhavāñ jetā yatir eṣā parājitā /
children.translated_text: "O learned one, you are the victor here; this female renunciant is defeated.

children.text: tad iyaṃ bhavataḥ śiṣyā bhaveta sarvadānugā || 120 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore let her be your disciple and follow you always." || <s>Svp</s>_120 ||

children.text: ekasminn eva divase mahādhīs tena nirjitā /
children.translated_text: "On a single day the greatly intelligent one was defeated by him —

children.text: katham atra saṃdeha iti sarve savismayāḥ || 121 ||
children.translated_text: how can there be any doubt here?" — so [said] all, with astonishment. || <s>Svp</s>_121 ||

children.text: iti sarvaiḥ samākhyātaṃ śrutvā sa brāhmaṇo mudā /
children.translated_text: Having heard what was declared by all, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with joy,

children.text: tāṃ parivrājikāṃ paśyan vihasann evam abravīt || 122 ||
children.translated_text: looking at that female mendicant, laughing, spoke thus: || <s>Svp</s>_122 ||
"O good woman, come along, as the agreement was made;
attaining the state of a follower, practice the <s>dharma</s> as my attendant." || <s>Svp</s>_123 ||

children.text: iti taduktam ākarṇya sā parivrājikā smitā /
children.translated_text: Hearing what he said, that female mendicant, smiling,
stood with downcast face, as if with a mind struck by shame. || <s>Svp</s>_124 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa mudito vipro daṇḍaṃ cchatram upānahaṃ /
children.translated_text: Then that delighted <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, giving her a staff, an umbrella, and sandals,
hastily summoning and consoling her, spoke thus: || <s>Svp</s>_125 ||

children.text: ayi bhadre tathā siddhaṃ yathā mayā samīhitaṃ /
children.translated_text: "O good woman, it has been accomplished just as I desired.

children.text: tat tvaṃ mudā mayā sārdhaṃ sukhaṃ cara samāvraja || 126 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, with joy, come along with me comfortably and happily." || <s>Svp</s>_126 ||

children.text: iti tat kathitaṃ śrutvā sā parivrājikā tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard what was said, that female mendicant then,

children.text: daṇḍam upānahau cchatraṃ gṛhītvā prasthitā śanaiḥ || 127 ||
children.translated_text: taking the staff, sandals, and umbrella, set forth slowly. || <s>Svp</s>_127 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa brāhmaṇo dhṛtvā tāṃ parivrājikāṃ mudā /
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, taking that female mendicant with joy,
with the exultation of the glory of victory, went to their dwelling. || <s>Svp</s>_128 ||
Having taken shelter in that dwelling, the learned man, greatly delighted,
enjoying himself as he wished together with her, lived happily. || <s>Svp</s>_129 ||
While she was thus enjoying herself there with that excessively passionate husband,
in time she became pregnant, like a rain-cloud [filled] with water in the monsoon. || <s>Svp</s>_130 ||
Then gradually that woman, with an increasingly growing womb,
became thin-limbed, pale-complexioned, soft-spoken, and slow in gait. || <s>Svp</s>_131 ||
Knowing herself to be pregnant, being censured by the people,
with a heart contracted by shame, she spoke to her husband, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: || <s>Svp</s>_132 ||

children.text: svāmin bhavān vijānātu yad ahaṃ garbhiṇī bhave /
children.translated_text: "My lord, may you understand that I have become pregnant.

children.text: tal lokair nindyamānātra kathaṃ careya sāṃprataṃ || 133 ||
children.translated_text: Being censured by the people here, how should I conduct myself now? || <s>Svp</s>_133 ||

children.text: tad anyaviṣaye gatvā sthātum icchati me manaḥ /
children.translated_text: My mind wishes to go and stay in another land.

children.text: yadīcchasi mayā sārdhaṃ rantuṃ prehi vrajevahi || 134 ||
children.translated_text: If you wish to enjoy life with me, come, let us depart." || <s>Svp</s>_134 ||

children.text: iti tayā samākhyātaṃ śrutvā sa brāhmaṇas tathā /
children.translated_text: Having heard what she said, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> likewise

children.text: anyatra viṣaye gantuṃ tayā sārdhaṃ samaicchata //135 //
children.translated_text: wished to go to another land together with her. || 135 ||

children.text: tatas tau mathurāṃ tyaktvā jagmatur dakṣiṇāpathaṃ /
children.translated_text: Then those two, leaving <s>Mathurā</s>, went to the southern region;
wandering on a journey through the countryside, they found happiness. || <s>Svp</s>_136 ||

children.text: tatra śvetavalākākhye pure tau dampatī mudā /
children.translated_text: There, in a city called <s>Śvetavalākā</s>, those two, husband and wife, joyfully
having arrived and taken shelter at night, rested, being weary. || <s>Svp</s>_137 ||
There, after the passing of nine months, when the time arrived,
in a rest-house at the edge of the public assembly hall, she gave birth to a small child. || <s>Svp</s>_138 ||
Beholding that son, golden and exceedingly beautiful,
that mother, with an astonished heart, stood with face bowed in modesty. || <s>Svp</s>_139 ||

children.text: janako' pi tam ālokya vijño 'yaṃ hi bhaved api /
children.translated_text: The father too, seeing him, [thought] 'indeed this one may become wise,'

children.text: iti matvā ciraṃ paśyans tasthau saṃharṣitāśayaḥ || 140 ||
children.translated_text: and thinking thus, gazing for a long time, stood with a delighted mind. || <s>Svp</s>_140 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa janakas tasya kṛtvā jātimahaṃ svayaṃ /
children.translated_text: Then that father, having himself performed the birth ceremony for him,

children.text: nāmāsya kiṃ kariṣye 'ham iti dhyātvaivam abravīt || 141 ||
children.translated_text: [wondered] 'What name shall I give him?' and having reflected, spoke thus: || <s>Svp</s>_141 ||

children.text: yat sabhāyāṃ prajāto 'yaṃ tenāsya nandanasya me /
children.translated_text: "Since this child of mine was born in the assembly hall (<s>sabhā</s>),

children.text: sabhika iti vikhyātaṃ nāma bhavatu sarvataḥ || 142 ||
children.translated_text: let the name '<s>Sabhika</s>' become renowned everywhere for this, my son." || <s>Svp</s>_142 ||

children.text: ity ākhyāya pitā tasya dārakasya yathārthataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus declared appropriately the name of that child,
the father, having given the well-known name '<s>Sabhika</s>,' went on his way. || <s>Svp</s>_143 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa dārako mātrā pitrāpi saṃprapālitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then that boy, nourished by his mother and father alike,
with fully developed faculties, quickly grew up, becoming charming. || <s>Svp</s>_144 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa sabhiko dhīmān aśikṣata lipīḥ kramāt /
children.translated_text: Then the wise <s>Sabhika</s> learned writing step by step;
having studied all the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), he quickly attained the status of a great debater. || <s>Svp</s>_145 ||
Thus, that conqueror of debaters, wise and skilled in all branches of knowledge,
wished to defeat all those who prided themselves on their learning. || <s>Svp</s>_146 ||
Then, having obtained permission from his parents, that exceedingly proud one,
having gone forth as a renunciant and taken the command of his teacher, practiced the vow of an ascetic. || <s>Svp</s>_147 ||

children.text: yasya mātā mahāprājñā vidyākaraḥ pitā tathā /
children.translated_text: His mother was greatly wise, and his father was a mine of learning;
therefore the proud <s>Sabhika</s> was himself skilled in all branches of knowledge. || <s>Svp</s>_148 ||

children.text: tataḥ sa mānino jetuṃ samudrāntika āśrame /
children.translated_text: Then that proud one, in order to conquer, went to a hermitage near the ocean
to meet the great sages, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and learned ones. || <s>Svp</s>_149 ||
There, having defeated all debaters in the exposition of all <s>śāstras</s>,
having attained victory, he went about greatly delighted. || <s>Svp</s>_150 ||
Then, going to another hermitage, <s>Sabhika</s> observed [the scholars],

children.text: tathā pravādinaḥ sarvāñ jitvā jayaṃ samāyayau || 151 ||
children.translated_text: and having likewise defeated all the disputants, he achieved victory. || <s>Svp</s>_151 ||

children.text: evaṃ sa sabhiko gatvā ṣoḍaśanagareṣv api /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Sabhika</s>, having gone to sixteen cities,
having defeated all the disputants, attained the glory and fame of victory. || <s>Svp</s>_152 ||
Then <s>Sabhika</s>, intoxicated with the pride of all learning,
in order to defeat all disputants, reflected thus in his mind: || <s>Svp</s>_153 ||
"That <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) is one of great supernatural knowledge, omniscient, an <s>Arhat</s>, lord of sages,
the conqueror of all debaters — so it is famed everywhere now. || <s>Svp</s>_154 ||

children.text: tad ahaṃ tasya munīndrasya jagacchāstur mahāmateḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I shall go to the hermitage of that lord of sages, the teacher of the world, the great-minded one,
in order to ascertain the distinction of his wisdom." || <s>Svp</s>_155 ||

children.text: jetuṃ na śakyate buddhaḥ kṣatriyātmaja eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddha</s> cannot be defeated — he is indeed the son of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>;

children.text: raṇakāle tu vīrās te kṣatriyāḥ śāstravaimukhāḥ || 156 ||
children.translated_text: but in the time of battle, those <s>Kṣatriya</s> warriors are averse to the scriptures. || <s>Svp</s>_156 ||

children.text: vidyākaro mama pitā mahādhīr jananī punaḥ /
children.translated_text: My father is a mine of learning, and my mother is greatly intelligent;
I myself have crossed the ocean of knowledge and am the dispeller of the pride of all debaters. || <s>Svp</s>_157 ||

children.text: iti sa sabhiko dhyātvā vārāṇasyāṃ jināśrame /
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, <s>Sabhika</s> went to the monastery of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror, i.e., the <s>Buddha</s>) in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
and wandering to the Deer Park (<s>Mṛgadāva</s>), having looked around, he approached. || <s>Svp</s>_158 ||
There he saw that lord of sages, seated on the assembly throne, surrounded by all the people,

children.text: dadarśa sa munīndraṃ taṃ pūrṇendum iva bhāskaraṃ || 159 ||
children.translated_text: shining like a full moon, like the sun. || <s>Svp</s>_159 ||
Seeing him, that greatly proud one, with a mind overwhelmed by wonder,
stood with mouth agape, gazing with motionless senses. || <s>Svp</s>_160 ||

children.text: tato dhairyaṃ samālambya madamānaṃ vihāya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, gathering his composure, abandoning his intoxication and pride,
bowing down, with joined palms, gazing, he approached. || <s>Svp</s>_161 ||

children.text: tatra sa samupāśritya tasya śāstur mahāmuneḥ /
children.translated_text: There, having taken shelter, before that teacher, the great sage,
bowing at his lotus feet, with joined palms, he sought refuge. || <s>Svp</s>_162 ||

children.text: tatra sa suprasannātmā sāñjaliḥ sa puraḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, with a well-pleased mind, with joined palms, standing before [him],

children.text: saṃbuddhaṃ taṃ mahābhijñaṃ saṃpaśyann evam abravīt || 163 ||
children.translated_text: looking at that <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) of great supernatural knowledge, he spoke thus: || <s>Svp</s>_163 ||
"O <s>Bhagavan</s> (Lord), may you know for what purpose I have come here;

children.text: tad bhavān me manovāñchāṃ saṃpūrayitum arhati || 164 ||
children.translated_text: may you deign to fulfill my heart's desire." || <s>Svp</s>_164 ||

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena śrutvā sa bhagvāñ jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard that entreaty by him, that blessed <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror),

children.text: taṃ sabhikaṃ samālokya vihasann evam ādiśat || 165 ||
children.translated_text: looking at that <s>Sabhika</s>, laughing, instructed him thus: || <s>Svp</s>_165 ||

children.text: śṛṇu sādho mahābhāga yadarthe tvam ihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Listen, O noble, fortunate one, for whatever purpose you have come here —
I shall fulfill that for you; declare your desire." [Svp 166]

children.text: ity ādiṣṭaṃ munīndreṇa śrutvā sa sabhiko mudā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction from the lord of sages, that <s>Sabhika</s> with joy,

children.text: bhagavantaṃ tam ālokya sāñjalir evam abravīt || 167 ||
children.translated_text: looking upon that Blessed One, spoke thus with joined palms: [Svp 167]

children.text: bhagavan bhavatā prāptaṃ kiṃ jñānaṃ kiṃ ca te vrataṃ /
children.translated_text: "O Blessed One, what knowledge have you attained, and what is your vow —

children.text: yat saṃbuddho bhavān khyāta etad ādeṣṭum arhati || 168 ||
children.translated_text: that you are proclaimed as Fully Awakened (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>)? You should declare this." [Svp 168]
Having heard that request, the destroyer of all pride and intoxication,

children.text: bhagavān sabhikaṃ drṣṭvā tad uttaram upādiśat || 169 ||
children.translated_text: the Blessed One, seeing <s>Sabhika</s>, instructed <s>Uttara</s> in response: [Svp 169]
"Ask <s>Uttara</s> about this matter, O <s>Sabhika</s>;
this one [i.e., Sabhika] is ignorant before the disciples, having grasped only a little instruction." [Svp 170]
Having heard the Omniscient One's words, the proud <s>Sabhika</s>,

children.text: nirmada uttaraṃ vijñaṃ papraccha sāñjaliḥ smitaḥ || 171 ||
children.translated_text: now freed of intoxication [of pride], asked the wise <s>Uttara</s>, with joined palms, smiling: [Svp 171]
"You have been commanded by the Blessed One; instruct me on this matter."
Requested with humility by him, [<s>Uttara</s>] instructed the answer for that purpose: [Svp 172]
"How are you ignorant, O <s>Sabhika</s>, skilled as you are in all learning?
Listen, I shall tell you briefly, with attention: [Svp 173]
One who, having taken the vow of the conduct of awakening (<s>bodhicaryāvrata</s>), and attaining supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>),

children.text: saṃbodhayati yaḥ sarvaṃ sa saṃbuddho nigadyate || 174 ||
children.translated_text: awakens all — he is called the Fully Awakened One (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>). [Svp 174]
Having abandoned the household — the abode of <s>Māra</s> — free from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), with senses conquered,
one who practices the vow of austerity for the benefit of all beings — [Svp 175]
he is an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), of purified self, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes);

children.text: saddharmaśrāvakaḥ saṃghaḥ sa yogī yatir ucyate || 176 ||
children.translated_text: a hearer of the true <s>Dharma</s>, part of the <s>Saṃgha</s> — he is called a <s>yogī</s> and ascetic (<s>yati</s>). [Svp 176]
Knowing the world to be an illusion (<s>māyā</s>), bearing the welfare of self and others,
having taken the vow of the conduct of awakening, one who acts for the world's benefit — [Svp 177]
he is a <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant), of great supernatural knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), the abode of auspicious glory and good qualities —
he is known as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>), the bearer of all <s>Dharma</s>-meanings. [Svp 178]

children.text: ity uttareṇa saṃdiṣṭaṃ śrutvā sa sabhikaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction from <s>Uttara</s>, that <s>Sabhika</s> again,

children.text: sāścarya uttaraṃ vijñaṃ praṇatvā ca nyavedayat || 179 ||
children.translated_text: with wonder, bowing to the wise <s>Uttara</s>, declared: [Svp 179]

children.text: uttarabrāhmaṇāḥ ke ca snātakāś ca kathaṃ dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>Uttara</s>, who are the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>? And how are the <s>Snātakas</s>? And the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>)?

children.text: vaidikāś ca kathaṃ viprāḥ śrotriyāś cāpi te kathaṃ || 180 ||
children.translated_text: And how are the <s>Vaidikas</s>? And the <s>Viprās</s> (learned ones)? And how are the <s>Śrotriyas</s>? [Svp 180]

children.text: kṣetrajñāś ca kathaṃ te 'pi kathaṃ ca brahmacārinaḥ /
children.translated_text: And how are the <s>Kṣetrajñas</s> (knowers of the field)? And the <s>Brahmacārins</s> (celibate students)?

children.text: ṛṣayaś ca parivrājā munayaś ca tapasvinaḥ || 181 ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers), the <s>Parivrājas</s> (wandering ascetics), the <s>Munis</s> (sages), and the <s>Tapasvis</s> (ascetics)? [Svp 181]

children.text: yatayo yoginaś cāpi kathaṃ kenāpi karmataḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Yatis</s> (renunciants) and <s>Yogins</s> — by what action [do they become so]?

children.text: etat karma samākhyāya saṃbodhayatu me manaḥ || 182 ||
children.translated_text: Explain these actions and awaken my mind." [Svp 182]
Thus requested by him, <s>Uttara</s>, the Brahman-monk,

children.text: taṃ sabhikaṃ samālokya vihasann evam ādiśat || 183 ||
children.translated_text: looking at that <s>Sabhika</s>, spoke smilingly thus: [Svp 183]
"Those who are of pure self, devoted to the <s>dharma</s> of non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), ascetics,
bound by pure restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), skilled in the practice of <s>yoga</s> — [Svp 184]

children.text: sādhu śṛṇu samādhāya yad etat praṣṭum icchasi /
children.translated_text: Listen well, with concentration, to what you wish to ask —

children.text: tat te mano'bhituṣṭaye vakṣyāmy ahaṃ samāsataḥ // Svp_*184A* //
children.translated_text: for the satisfaction of your mind, I shall speak briefly: [Svp 184A]

children.text: yo viśvaṃ sṛjati brahmā svayaṃbhūr vedabhṛd vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: He who creates the universe — <s>Brahmā</s>, the Self-born, bearer of the <s>Vedas</s>, the Ordainer (<s>Vidhi</s>) —
his offspring, of righteous conduct, <s>sāttvika</s> (pure), with unstained senses — [Svp 184B]
of equal conduct toward self and others, dwelling in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes),
bearers of the meaning of Vedic <s>dharma</s>, virtuous — they are called <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. [Svp 185]

children.text: snātvā tīrtheṣu nityaṃ ye śuddhaśīlā jitendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, always bathing at sacred fords (<s>tīrtha</s>), of pure conduct, with conquered senses,

children.text: brahmavrataṃ carantas te niṣkāṃkṣāḥ snātakāḥ smṛtāḥ || 186 ||
children.translated_text: practicing the vow of <s>Brahman</s>, free from longing — they are called <s>Snātakas</s> (graduated students). [Svp 186]
Those who are purified by sacraments (<s>saṃskāra</s>), practicing Vedic <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: brahmacaryāvrataṃ dhṛtvā carante te dvijāḥ smṛtāḥ || 187 ||
children.translated_text: having taken the vow of celibate study (<s>brahmacarya</s>) and practicing it — they are called the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>). [Svp 187]
Of pure conduct and behavior, accomplishing the purpose of Vedic <s>dharma</s>,
established in the livelihood of <s>Brahman</s>, steadfast — they are called <s>Vaidikas</s> (Vedic scholars). [Svp 188]

children.text: ye brahmasaṃvaraṃ dhṛtvā saṃcarantaḥ sadā śubhe /
children.translated_text: Those who, holding the restraint of <s>Brahman</s>, always walking in the auspicious,

children.text: sadvidheḥ pūrayanty arthaṃ te viprāḥ kathitā budhaiḥ || 189 ||
children.translated_text: fulfilling the purpose of the True Ordainer — they are called <s>Viprās</s> (learned ones) by the wise. [Svp 189]
Those who are very steadfast, of great heroism, striving for the welfare of all beings,
bearers of the auspicious meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, wise — they are called <s>Śrotriyas</s> (learned in scripture). [Svp 190]

children.text: sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ yat kṣetram ātmā samāśrayet /
children.translated_text: He who understands the purification of that field which the self pervades

children.text: tadviśuddhiṃ vijānīte sa tu kṣetrajña ucyate || 191 ||
children.translated_text: as the field of all the senses — he is called the <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field). [Svp 191]
Those whose selves are [imbued] with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), whose minds are moistened with compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>),

children.text: upekṣya saṃcarante 'rthe bhadra te brahmacārinaḥ // Svp_l92 //
children.translated_text: who move with equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) in purpose, auspicious — they are the <s>Brahmacārins</s> (celibate students). [Svp 192]
Those whose zeal is turned from <s>saṃsāra</s>, who long for the bliss of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation),
who practice the vow of renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>) — they are called <s>Parivrājakas</s> (wandering ascetics). [Svp 193]
Those of <s>Brahman</s>-like conduct, great beings, of great supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>),
attaining the path to heaven — they are called <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers). [Svp 194]
Those who are unattached to the course of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>), with well-established senses,
practicing the conduct of silence (<s>mauna</s>), virtuous — they are called <s>Munis</s> (sages). [Svp 195]
Those who, indifferent even to their own bodies, practice the vow of austerity (<s>tapas</s>) —
seekers of auspicious glory and good qualities — they are called <s>Tapasvis</s> (ascetics). [Svp 196]
Those who are free from longing for the delights of illusion (<s>māyā</s>), without afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), with conquered senses,
without possessiveness, of controlled selves — they are the <s>Yatis</s> (ascetics), unstained. [Svp 197]
Those of faithful conduct, free from conceptual thought (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), without attachment,
with selves established in <s>samādhi</s> (meditation) — they are the <s>Yogins</s>, unstained. [Svp 198]
These, freed from worldly existence, practitioners of the renunciation vow,
of purified senses and selves — they attain the supreme goal (<s>paramā gati</s>). [Svp 199]

children.text: etat svalpatarārthe 'pi kathaṃ na jñāyate tvayā /
children.translated_text: Even this minor matter — how is it not known by you?
Puffed up with the pride of learning, [thinking] 'I shall conquer all,' intoxicated with arrogance — [Svp 200]

children.text: mānaṃ tyaja tvaṃ sabhika bhajainaṃ śāstrapāragaṃ /
children.translated_text: Abandon your pride, O <s>Sabhika</s>; worship this one who has crossed to the far shore of the scriptures.
Pursue awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), O seeker of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — take up the vow of renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>)." [Svp 201]
Having spoken thus, he narrated in detail his own story —
and the majesty of <s>Nālaka</s>'s younger brother [i.e., the Buddha], the Omniscient One. [Svp 202]
"This one alone, in the three worlds, is the lord of all knowledge, the wise one —
the lord of all <s>dharma</s>, the Teacher (<s>Śāstṛ</s>), the destroyer of the pride of all debaters. [Svp 203]
By the mere remembrance of whom, my younger brother, of great wisdom,
became the conqueror of all debaters, the upholder of scripture, having fully crossed over. [Svp 204]
When even the sight and hearing of such an Omniscient One [has such power],

children.text: kā kathā cara tasmāt tvaṃ śāsane 'sya susaṃvaraṃ || 205 ||
children.translated_text: what more need be said? Therefore, practice well-restrained conduct under his teaching." [Svp 205]
Having heard <s>Uttara</s>'s words, that exceedingly bold <s>Sabhika</s>
became eager and determined to take up the vow of renunciation. [Svp 206]

children.text: iti tena jagacchāstrā samādiṣṭaṃ niśamya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the instruction given by that Teacher of the world,
<s>Sabhika</s>, with a very serene mind, rejoiced greatly, being enlightened. [Svp 206*]
Then that wise <s>Sabhika</s>, longing for the qualities of the Fully Awakened One,

children.text: taṃ munīndraṃ mudā natvā sāñjalir evam abravīt || 207 ||
children.translated_text: bowing joyfully to that lord of sages, spoke thus with joined palms: [Svp 207]
"O Blessed One (<s>Bhagavan</s>), Omniscient, Wise, who has crossed to the far shore of all knowledge —
forgive my offense born of pride, O treasure of compassion (<s>dayānidhi</s>). [Svp 208]

children.text: tvam eva bhagavān nāthaḥ sarvadharmādhipo jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: You alone are the Blessed Lord, the Protector (<s>Nātha</s>), the lord of all <s>dharma</s>, the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>).
You alone are the Teacher of the world, of great supernatural knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), the lord of sages. [Svp 209]
The conqueror of the four <s>Māras</s>, the Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> —
you alone shine as the sovereign lord of the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>). [Svp 210]
The destroyer of the darkness of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), the sun of the knowledge of true <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: yad ahaṃ bhagavan pātuṃ dharmāmṛtaṃ samutsahe || 211 ||
children.translated_text: I, O Blessed One, am eager to drink the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) of the <s>dharma</s>. [Svp 211]

children.text: tad bhavān māṃ samālokya samanvāhartum arhati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should look upon me and accept me.
I, always instructed by you, have come to your refuge (<s>śaraṇa</s>). [Svp 212]
Having received your permission and having established myself, I shall practice the Buddhist (<s>Saugata</s>) path.
Therefore, in the Buddhist <s>dharma</s>, the means of attaining auspicious, glorious awakening — [Svp 213]
with compassion, you should unite me [with the path] and set me in motion."

children.text: iti saṃprārthitaṃ tena śrutvā sa karuṇāmbudhiḥ || 214 ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this request from him, that ocean of compassion (<s>karuṇāmbhudhi</s>), [Svp 214]
seeing that wanderer freed from pride, instructed thus:

children.text: ehi bhadrāsti te vāṃcchā saugate saṃvare yadi || 215 ||
children.translated_text: "Come, O good one; if your desire is for Buddhist restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), [Svp 215]
establish yourself in the conduct of awakening (<s>bodhicaryā</s>) and practice the vow free from afflictions."

children.text: ity ādiśya sa saṃbuddho dakṣiṇapāṇinā svayaṃ || 216 ||
children.translated_text: Having instructed thus, the Fully Awakened One (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>), with his own right hand, [Svp 216]
touching his head, purified his three bodies (<s>trikāya</s>).

children.text: bhagavatā śiraḥ spṛṣṭe muṇḍitaḥ sa jitendriyaḥ || 217 ||
children.translated_text: When his head was touched by the Blessed One, he became tonsured, with conquered senses, [Svp 217]
bearing a bowl, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), clothed in robes.
Then he, of very serene mind, having received the permission of the Teacher of the world, [Svp 218]
having taken the vow of the conduct of awakening (<s>bodhicaryāvrata</s>), practiced [the path] with concentration.
Then, with his mind purified by <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), with the three spheres completely purified,
the <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), possessing great supernatural knowledge, became a Buddhist <s>yati</s> (ascetic). || Svp 219 ||

body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, called the chapter on the observance and practice of going forth into the Buddhist teaching of <s>Sabhika</s>, in the glorious <s>Bhadrakalpāvadāna</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Upagupta</s>.

children.translated_text: (SAM 47a3ff.: additional verses):

children.text: etad dṛṣṭvā samākarṇya sarve lokādhipā api /
children.translated_text: Having seen and heard this, all the lords of the world also,
approving of that vow, practiced it with delight. || Svp *219* ||

children.text: iti me guruṇādiṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mayā tathocyate /
children.translated_text: Thus what was instructed to me by the guru, having been heard by me, is thus spoken;

children.text: tvam apīdaṃ mahārāja śrutvānumodya cāraya // Svp_*22O* //
children.translated_text: you too, O great king, having heard and approved, should practice this. || Svp *220* ||
Having heard this, may all those of pure faculties approve of me;
may the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural knowledge attain enlightenment. || Svp *221* ||
Having heard this instruction given by the venerable teacher, king <s>Aśoka</s> with joy,
having approved, saying "so be it," rejoiced together with his assembly. || Svp *222* ||

body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, called the chapter on the observance and practice of going forth into the Buddhist teaching of <s>Sabhika</s>.
